symmetryCheck: Polavaram across regimes: the same lens (contract switch, single-bidder, donor record) was run on the Congress-era award (Transstroy JV, 2 Mar 2013), the TDP-era award (Navayuga, 27 Feb 2018; Bekem, Dec 2018) and the YSRCP-era award (MEIL, 8 Nov 2019). CAG's 2025 audit finds rule violations in all three eras — nomination-basis awards with revised estimates, interest-free Special Revolving Fund/Imprest to contract agencies, and the single-bidder reverse tender — and Navayuga (Rs 55 cr) as well as MEIL (Rs 584 cr) bought bonds encashed by BJP. The lens produces an equally alarming picture for each government; the discriminating finding is systemic (AP irrigation contracting repeatedly favours large Hyderabad EPC firms whichever party governs), not partisan. Teesta across regimes: the SDF government (Chamling) selected Teesta Urja in 2005 with a private lead (Athena) and raised the state stake to 60.08% in 2015 while the cost rose from Rs 5,705 cr to Rs 13,965 cr; the SKM government (Tamang) divested that stake to Greenko in 2024 after the collapse. Both regimes made large, non-competitive decisions in favour of a private partner; the BJP, an ally of SKM, is petitioning against the SKM decision, so the challenge is not a simple opposition narrative. PSP control: Maharashtra's 7 Jun 2023 MoUs went to a CPSU (NHPC, 7,350 MW) as well as to Torrent (5,700 MW); SECI's 2026 auction awarded the same private names (Greenko, Torrent, Tata). Nomination is the default channel for public and private developers alike; the method, not the beneficiary, generates the pattern.
